reasons: The inserted Section 10.3 sits correctly at the end of the termination-effects section (after 10.2) and tracks the preferred position: up to six months' transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates, return of Customer Data in a commonly used machine-readable format within thirty days, and certified deletion thereafter.
The edit is purely additive — the existing text of p0042 is untouched — which is the smallest edit capable of curing a 'missing' provision.

The comment accurately describes the gap (Section 10 covers only access wind-down and Deliverables), states what was added, and offers the playbook fallback (90 days) while preserving the 30-day export and deletion certification; tone and prefix conform.

Minor drafting deltas ('within thirty days of Customer's request'; deletion 'subject to routine backups and legal retention requirements') are commercially standard qualifiers that do not fall to the walk-away line (no data return or immediate deletion), so they do not defeat the rule; flag only if the reviewer wants the 30-day clock to run automatically from termination.
